when: a dragon is due within about a minute
asks: where do I ward for dragon
drake's coming, do I ward
should I go ward river now
dragon soon where's my ward go
say: Shove the wave and ward river with your marksman following, or keep the wards and hold lane if you're pinned under tower.
more: Wards placed before the spawn are the ones that count. They show which way their jungler and mid are walking, so your team can decide to fight or give it.
Going with the wave pushed means their bot lane has to choose between minions and following you.
If you leave a marksman alone under tower to ward, they can dive him, and you lose more than the dragon.
check: Is your wave pushed past the middle, and where was their jungler last seen?
breaks: Wrong if their bot lane is missing or your jungler is on the top side: stay with your marksman and ward only the brush next to lane.
basis: pro:The lane that pushes first moves first

when: a dragon or baron is due within about a minute and your support item holds wards
asks: should I swap to sweeper
do I sweep before dragon
when do I use my sweeper
red trinket or keep wards
should I be clearing wards
say: Sweep the pit and the brush on your side first, then ward their entrances, or only ward if your team isn't with you yet.
more: Clearing their vision first means they can't see who's there or when you start. That makes them walk in blind, and a blind walk is where picks come from.
Your own wards go further out, on the paths they must take, so you get a few seconds of warning.
Sweeping takes time standing still in the dark. It's a job for when teammates are close enough to answer.
check: Is at least one teammate within reach of you, and is your trinket the sweeper?
breaks: Wrong if you're the only one near the river: drop one ward from a safe spot and wait for the team instead of sweeping alone.

when: your team has more kills and more towers than theirs
asks: where do I ward when we're ahead
we're winning, where's vision go
should I ward their jungle
deep wards or no
say: Ward their jungle entrances and buff with your jungler beside you, or keep wards on the river if he's on the other side.
more: When you're ahead, deep wards turn the lead into picks: you see them leave base and choose who to catch.
The deeper the ward, the earlier you know which objective they're walking to, which lets your team be there first.
River wards are the fallback. They don't find picks, but they stop the one mistake that gives a lead back, which is being surprised.
check: Where is your jungler right now, and which enemies are showing on the map?
breaks: Wrong if three or more enemies are missing: a deep ward walk is the comeback they're waiting for, so ward the river and stay grouped.
basis: pro:When ahead, let them come to you

when: their team has more kills and more towers than yours
asks: where do I ward when we're behind
we're losing, where do wards go
I keep dying trying to ward
safe wards when behind
say: Ward your own jungle entrances and the brush beside your towers, or go one step further only with two teammates walking with you.
more: When you're behind, their team owns the river. A ward there costs your life and tells you very little you can act on.
Wards in your own jungle show them coming, and that's what lets your carries farm safely until their items arrive.
It also sets up the one good thing a losing team gets: catching someone who walks into your side too deep.
check: Which of your outer towers are still standing, and who can actually walk with you?
breaks: Wrong if a soul-point dragon or baron is about to be taken for free: then the team has to move together and you ward as a group on the way.

when: you have gold and are about to recall
asks: should I buy a pink ward
do I get a control ward
is a control ward worth it
where do I put my control ward
say: Buy a control ward every recall and put it where your team will fight next, or beside your carry's lane if nothing's spawning soon.
more: A control ward does two jobs: it shows the area and it switches off their wards near it. One in the right brush can last minutes.
Placed on the side of the next objective, it's already working before anyone arrives.
Placed near a lane, it's protection against ganks, which matters more when no objective is close.
check: Do you already have one alive on the map, and which objective spawns next?
breaks: Wrong if you're one small purchase from finishing an item that keeps your carry alive in the next fight: finish that first, then go back to buying them.

when: your jungler is dead
asks: can I go ward alone
is it safe to ward right now
jungler's dead, do I still ward
should I walk into river by myself
say: Stay with your carry until your jungler's back, or ward only as far as your nearest tower covers if you really need the sight.
more: With your jungler dead, theirs is free to hunt, and a support walking alone to ward is the easiest kill on the map.
Dying now doesn't just cost you. It leaves your carry alone and the next objective a player short.
Vision can wait thirty seconds. Arriving with a second body makes the same ward safe.
check: How long is your jungler's respawn timer, and which enemies are showing?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler and support are both dead too: then the river is empty and it's the best time to ward deep.
basis: pro:Before a spawn, arrive alive and on time

when: game time is past 20:00, baron is alive and your team is ahead in kills and towers
asks: how do I ward baron
where's vision go for baron
we want baron, what do I ward
baron wards when ahead
say: Sweep the pit, then ward their jungle paths into it with the team beside you, or just hold river brush if someone's still farming.
more: Baron takes a while and bunches your team up. The danger isn't the pit itself, it's who arrives through their jungle while you're in it.
Wards on their approach paths tell your team to stop and turn before a steal or a flank can happen.
With a lead you don't need to rush it. Vision first, then a pick, then the baron is the safe order.
check: Is their jungler alive, and are all five of you on the top side?
breaks: Wrong if a teammate is alone on the bot side: the enemy can simply fight four against five, so wait for the group before you walk in.
basis: pro:With a lead, Baron is bait before it is a prize

when: game time is past 20:00, baron is alive and your team is behind in kills and towers
asks: how do I stop them taking baron
we're behind, baron vision?
do I ward baron when losing
they're gonna sneak baron what do I do
say: Keep one ward looking into the pit from your side, or throw a control ward in river brush if you can't get that close.
more: When you're behind, the goal isn't to own the pit. It's to know the moment they start, so your team can decide to contest together or take something elsewhere.
One ward that sees the pit is worth more than three deep ones you died placing.
If they start it and you can't fight, that's the cue for a tower or dragon on the other side.
check: Which enemies are missing from the map, and how many teammates are near you?
breaks: Wrong if four or five enemies are missing at once: don't walk up to check, assume they're there and ping the team to group or trade.
basis: pro:If you cannot contest, take something elsewhere at once

when: one team has four dragons and the elder dragon is due
asks: how do I ward for elder
elder's spawning, vision?
where do I stand for elder dragon
elder setup as support
say: Recall, buy control wards and reach the pit early with everyone, or defend the entrances from your side if you're the weaker team.
more: Elder usually decides the game, so everything before it is about arriving first, alive and with wards in hand.
The team that's there early sweeps and makes the other walk through dark brush into them.
If you're weaker, holding a narrow entrance on your side gives your team a better fight than walking into the open river.
check: How long until it spawns, and does anyone on your team still need to recall?
breaks: Wrong if baron is up and the enemy is all showing at the dragon side: your team can start baron instead and make them choose.
basis: pro:A second objective moves the fight

when: an ally in a side lane has more CS than anyone else and the rest of your team is grouped
asks: our top is split pushing, where do I ward
how do I help the split pusher
vision for a side lane
do I ward for the guy pushing
say: Ward the jungle paths between mid and his lane so he sees them coming, or stay grouped mid if your four can't hold alone.
more: A split pusher only works if he knows how many are walking at him. Your ward on the path gives him the seconds to back off.
When they send two or three, that ward also tells your group it's safe to start an objective or push mid.
If your four lose a fight without you, the split means nothing, so the group comes first.
check: How many enemies are showing mid, and does your split pusher have Teleport?
breaks: Wrong if a dragon or baron spawns in under a minute: vision belongs at the pit, and he should be pushing the lane on the opposite side.
basis: pro:Push the side waves before you posture at Baron

when: an enemy assassin has several more kills than deaths
asks: their assassin keeps killing us
how do I ward against the fed assassin
we keep getting flanked
where do I ward so we don't get picked
say: Put wards on the side brush and behind your team, not in front, or stand next to your carry if you're out of wards.
more: A fed assassin doesn't come through the front. He waits to the side until the fight starts, then goes for the back.
A ward on the flank turns his best play into a wasted walk, and often into a kill for you when he's seen early.
Without wards, your body is the vision. Standing with the carry means he has to go through your crowd control first.
check: Is the assassin showing on the map right now, and which side brush is dark?
breaks: Wrong if he's dead or showing far away: use that window to ward forward instead, toward the next objective.

when: game time is between 7:00 and 8:00
asks: should I go ward for grubs
grubs are coming, do I go top
do I leave bot for grubs
grub vision as support
say: Stay bot and keep the dragon side warded, or walk up for grubs only if your wave is shoved and your marksman's safe.
more: Grubs are one early window and don't come back, so it's tempting to go. But a support walking top leaves a marksman alone for a long time.
Often the better trade is the mirror one: your jungler's top side, so you ward dragon and take it if theirs shows up there.
Going is right when the lane is already won and nothing can punish your marksman.
check: Is your wave pushed in, how healthy is your marksman, and did their support leave too?
breaks: Wrong if their support has already left lane toward the top side: follow or ping it, because your jungler is about to be outnumbered.
basis: pro:Price grubs against plates and waves

when: an outer tower fell in the last minute
asks: tower's down, where do I ward now
we lost our tower, where's vision
we took their tower, do I ward deeper
where do wards go after towers fall
say: If you took theirs, ward the jungle behind it with your team; if you lost yours, ward your own jungle behind where it stood.
more: A tower is safe ground. When it falls, the jungle next to it changes hands, and wards should move with it.
After taking one, the camps and paths behind it are where their team now walks unseen, so that's where you look for picks.
After losing one, your carries can't farm that side safely until your own jungle there is lit.
check: Which tower fell, and which objective is on that side of the map?
breaks: Wrong if the fallen tower is on the opposite side from the next objective: put your wards at the objective first and fix that side later.

asks: I'm out of wards
no wards left, what do I do
should I recall for wards
my wards are on cooldown
say: Recall for wards now if an objective is over a minute away, or stay grouped and sweep instead if it's about to spawn.
more: A recall refills your wards and lets you buy control wards. Done early, you're back before anything starts.
Done late, you're the missing fifth when the fight happens, which is worse than having no wards.
Sweeping still helps without wards of your own. Taking theirs away evens out what each side can see.
check: How long until the next dragon or baron, and how much gold do you have?
breaks: Wrong if your team is about to fight right now: stay, and use your body to check brush only with the tank next to you.
basis: pro:Before a spawn, arrive alive and on time

when: you died in the last 30 seconds
asks: I got caught warding
I died placing a ward
how do I stop dying when I ward
every time I ward I get killed
say: Next time ward on the way back from base with a teammate walking the same way, or ward one brush shorter when you're alone.
more: Most support deaths while warding happen at the furthest ward, alone, when enemies were missing from the map.
Warding as you walk out from base means you're healthy and your team is usually moving with you.
One brush shorter gives a little less information and is far safer. A ward that's placed beats a deeper one you died for.
check: Before you step forward: how many enemies can you see on the map?
breaks: Wrong if the enemy who killed you is now dead or showing on the far side: the area is open, so go back and finish the ward.

when: the enemy team has a champion with camouflage or invisibility
asks: how do I ward against stealth
their invisible guy keeps getting us
do control wards show stealth
I can't see him coming
say: Keep a control ward where your carry stands in fights, or carry the sweeper and use it when your team stops to siege.
more: A control ward reveals camouflaged champions near it, so one in the brush beside your back line takes away the surprise.
The sweeper does a similar job on the move, but only for a short time, so save it for when you expect him.
The carry who can see the stealth champion first usually wins that exchange.
check: Has their stealth champion been seen in the last few seconds, and where is your carry standing?
breaks: Wrong if he's dead: spend that window on forward wards instead of defensive ones.

when: a dragon or baron is due and the enemy team has more engage than yours
asks: they have way more engage, how do I ward
how do I stop us getting flanked at dragon
we're a poke team, where do wards go
they keep jumping on us at objectives
say: Ward the flanks and the brush behind your team rather than the pit, or hold a control ward on your carries' spot.
more: An engage team wins by reaching your back line from an angle you didn't see. Flank wards make them come through the front, where your poke is waiting.
It also suits you to arrive first and let them start the objective, since a team hitting it is clumped in a small space.
Pit vision matters less to you than knowing where their engager is standing.
check: Where is their main engager right now, and which side paths are dark?
breaks: Wrong if their engager is dead or showing in a far lane: push forward and take the pit vision while the threat is gone.
basis: pro:Who starts the objective depends on who wants to be pinned

when: a dragon is due in about a minute
asks: dragon in a minute, what do I do
how do I set up for drake as support
should I back before dragon
do I recall or stay for dragon
say: Recall now so you walk in with full wards and health, or stay and ward right away if you're already healthy.
more: A recall a minute out gets you back in time with wards and a control ward. A recall thirty seconds out makes you late.
Being first into the river is what the setup is for: your team wards, theirs has to walk in blind.
Don't take a risky trade in this minute. A death now costs the whole dragon, not just the kill.
check: How many wards and how much health and mana do you have right now?
breaks: Wrong if your team isn't going to contest at all: then use the minute to ward your own jungle and push a wave instead.
basis: pro:Before a spawn, arrive alive and on time

when: their jungler is dead and a dragon or baron is up
asks: their jungler's dead, what now
jungler died, do we take dragon
should we do baron, their jungle's dead
we killed the jungler
say: Ping your team onto the objective now while they have no Smite, or sweep and ward it first if his timer is long.
more: The jungler is the kill that matters most near an objective. Without him, they have no reliable way to steal it.
Your job is to make it fast and safe: sweep the pit, stand between it and their side, and call out anyone walking in.
A long timer gives you seconds to clear vision properly. A short one means start immediately.
check: How long is his respawn timer, and is your own jungler alive and near?
breaks: Wrong if your jungler is dead or far away too: without Smite on your side it's slow and stealable by anyone, so take a tower instead.
basis: pro:A dead jungler makes the objective free

when: their support is dead and an objective is up or due within a minute
asks: their support's dead, what do I do
we killed their support
support died, do we go drake
can I ward deep now their support's down
say: Sweep every ward near the objective while he can't replace them, or push the nearest wave first if your team's far away.
more: A dead support means their vision stops being refreshed. Whatever you clear now stays dark until he's back.
That's the cheapest moment to make the pit yours: clear, then ward their entrances.
It also means their carry has nobody peeling, so a fight near the pit favors you for the next while.
check: How long is his respawn timer, and is the sweeper your trinket?
breaks: Wrong if your own carries are dead too: you can't use the darkness, so just place defensive wards and reset.

when: your health is low and an objective is due within a minute
asks: I'm low, do I stay for dragon
no mana, should I back before the fight
do I recall or help with drake
I'm half health and dragon's spawning
say: Recall right now and walk back with the team, or stay far back and only drop wards if there's no time left.
more: A support at low health or without mana can't engage, can't peel and gets picked first. The other team will start the fight on you.
Recalling early costs a few seconds of vision. Recalling late or dying costs the objective.
If there's truly no time, your wards and your presence still count, as long as you stay where nobody can reach you.
check: Exactly how long until it spawns, and are enemies already in the river?
breaks: Wrong if the fight has already started: a recall now just removes you, so stay behind your carry and use what you have.
basis: pro:Before a spawn, arrive alive and on time

when: the enemy team has three dragons and the next one is due within two minutes
asks: they're on soul point
they have three drakes, what do I do
how do we stop soul
soul dragon's coming, setup?
say: Group at the pit a full minute early with wards and control wards, or trade for baron if you can't win that fight.
more: Dragons given earlier bought your team time. This is the one that has to be contested, because soul makes every later fight harder.
Getting there early matters more here than anywhere: sweep, ward their paths, and make them walk into you.
If the fight is hopeless, losing soul and getting nothing is the worst result. Baron or towers at the same moment is the alternative.
check: Is baron up, and are your carries' main items finished?
breaks: Wrong if two of your teammates are dead when it spawns: don't walk in as three, defend towers and look for the trade.
basis: pro:Give early dragons, then fight the one before soul point

when: your team has three dragons and the next one is due within two minutes
asks: we're on soul point, how do I set up
one more drake for soul
soul's next, what's my job
how do we secure soul
say: Push mid, recall together, then take the river early and wait, or look for a pick on whoever comes to ward.
more: With soul point in hand, you don't need a coin flip. They have to come to you, through vision you control.
Their support and jungler must walk in to ward, and that's the pick that makes the dragon free.
Spend gold first. A lead sitting in your pocket doesn't help in the fight.
check: Does your team have unspent gold, and is the mid wave pushed?
breaks: Wrong if a side wave is about to crash into your inhibitor tower: send one player to clear it first, or they'll trade for your base.
basis: pro:A lead is not power until it is spent

when: game time is past 20:00, baron is alive and their jungler is alive
asks: should we start baron
do we rush baron
baron or wait
how do I help set up baron
say: Have the team tap baron to pull them in, then turn and fight, or finish it only after you've caught someone.
more: With their jungler alive, a straight baron is a Smite gamble. Using it as bait makes them walk through dark jungle to stop you.
As support, you stand on their side of the pit with wards out, ready to stop the first player who appears.
After a pick, the same baron is safe, because they're a player short and can't force the fight.
check: Is the pit swept, and where was their jungler last seen?
breaks: Wrong if your team is behind: bait doesn't work when they'd win the fight anyway, so only start it when their jungler is dead.
basis: pro:With a lead, Baron is bait before it is a prize

when: game time is between 7:30 and 9:00 and no dragon is due within a minute
asks: grubs or stay bot
should I help my jungler with grubs
jungler's doing grubs, do I go
do I rotate top for grubs
say: Stay bot and take plates with your marksman while they're busy top, or go if their support has already left lane.
more: Grubs only pay off if your team later reaches towers. Plates and waves bot are gold you get for certain.
If their support walks up and you don't, your jungler fights outnumbered. That's the one reason to match.
A partial take is fine. Nobody needs to die to get all of them.
check: Has their support left the lane, and how healthy is their tower?
breaks: Wrong if your marksman is weak and their duo can dive him alone: stay with him, or bring him with you rather than splitting up.
basis: pro:Price grubs against plates and waves

when: your bot laner is dead and a dragon is up or due within 30 seconds
asks: my adc's dead and dragon's up
adc died, do we still fight for drake
we're down our carry, dragon?
do we give dragon
say: Give this dragon and take a tower or their camps on the top side, or just ward and clear waves until he's back.
more: Fighting an objective without your main damage dealer is slow on the dragon and weak in the fight.
Giving it is fine as long as you're paid for it. Start the trade the moment they start the dragon.
If nothing is available to trade, staying alive with waves cleared means you've only lost the one dragon.
check: How long is his respawn timer, and is this their soul-point dragon?
breaks: Wrong if it's their soul dragon and he respawns in time to walk there: stall at the entrance with wards and wait for him.
basis: pro:If you cannot contest, take something elsewhere at once

when: a dragon or baron is up and both junglers are alive
asks: what do I do at the pit
how do I help my jungler get the smite
who do I use my stuff on at dragon
do I engage or zone at baron
say: Use your crowd control on their jungler when the objective is low, or engage on their carries if he's already out of range.
more: The last hit is a contest between two players. If theirs is stunned or pushed away at that moment, it isn't a contest.
This matters most when their jungler bursts monsters harder than yours.
If he isn't nearby, your engage is better spent starting the fight on your terms while they're watching the pit.
check: Where is their jungler standing, and how low is the objective?
breaks: Wrong if their team is collapsing on your back line: forget the jungler and peel, since a secured dragon with a lost fight costs more.
basis: pro:If you cannot win the Smite duel, remove their jungler

when: a dragon or baron is up
asks: where do I stand at dragon
where's an enchanter go during baron
do I stand in the pit
how do I position at the objective
say: Stand between your carry and their side so you can shield or stop the first diver, or step out to ward if it's quiet.
more: A team hitting an objective is packed together. The enemy's best play is to jump the carry from the open side.
If you're already standing there, your shield or crowd control lands before the damage does.
Stepping out to place a ward is worth it only while no enemy is close, since you're the easiest target alone.
check: Which direction are they coming from, and how many are showing?
breaks: Wrong if their team has long-range poke rather than divers: spread out instead, so one ability doesn't hit all of you.

when: a dragon or baron is due within a minute
asks: how do I play dragon as a mage support
do I poke or wait at drake
what's my job at the objective with poke
should we start it or let them
say: Get there first and poke them as they walk in, or let them start it and hit them while they're bunched in the pit.
more: Your damage works best on a team that has to come through a narrow path or stand still on a monster.
If your team starts it instead, you're the ones clumped up, and their engage gets an easy target.
Every bit of health you take off before the fight makes them think twice about contesting.
check: Who got to the river first, and do they have hard engage that can reach you?
breaks: Wrong if you're late and they hold the brush: don't walk up to poke into the dark, wait for your tank to check it first.
basis: pro:Who starts the objective depends on who wants to be pinned

when: herald or baron and a dragon are both up or due within a minute of each other
asks: two objectives up, which do I go to
dragon or herald
which side do I ward
baron and dragon both up
say: Go with your jungler and carry to whichever one they pick, or ward the other on your way so you see them start.
more: When two objectives are up, the team that splits its support from its carries loses both.
One ward on the objective you're not taking tells you whether they're trading or coming to fight.
If they start the far one, yours is free, so finish it fast rather than running across the map late.
check: Which side are your jungler and strongest carry on?
breaks: Wrong if their whole team shows at yours: don't fight outnumbered for it, swap to the other one immediately.
basis: pro:A second objective moves the fight

when: an enemy died in the last 20 seconds and a dragon or baron is up
asks: we got a pick, now what
we killed one, do we go objective
pick into what
should we chase or take dragon
say: Stop chasing and move the team onto the objective, or take a tower instead if their jungler's the one still alive nearby.
more: A kill is only worth what you buy with it. The numbers advantage lasts as long as the death timer.
You're often the one who sees this first, because you're not the one chasing. Ping it early.
If the dead player is their jungler, it's nearly free. If their jungler's alive, a tower is the safer payment.
check: Who died, how long is the timer, and is your jungler healthy?
breaks: Wrong if your team is low after the fight: recall and spend the gold, then set up the objective with full health.
basis: pro:After a won fight, the waves decide whether you got paid

asks: do I engage or peel
what's my job in teamfights
should I go in
do I start the fight or stay back
say: Engage when your damage dealers are close enough to follow, or hold your crowd control for whoever dives your carry.
more: Your engage only works if damage arrives with it. Going in while your carries are far back just gets you killed first.
If their team has divers, the better use of the same abilities is on the diver, after he commits.
A good rule is to look at your team before you look at theirs: who can actually follow right now.
check: Where are your carries standing, and who on their team wants to jump in?
breaks: Wrong if your team is behind and can't win a straight fight: only engage on someone caught alone.

asks: who do I stay with in fights
what do I do in teamfights as an enchanter
who do I shield
where do I stand in fights
say: Stand a step behind your strongest carry and save your best ability for when he's dived, or buff whoever's doing the damage.
more: Your value is keeping one important player alive and hitting. Spread across five people, your shields and heals do little.
Holding the key ability until the dive comes is hard but it's what wins the fight. Used early, the diver just waits.
If nobody's diving, the same spells go to whoever is dealing damage.
check: Who on your team has the most items, and who on theirs is looking to jump in?
breaks: Wrong if your strongest carry is dead or not in the fight: switch at once to the next best damage dealer rather than following a tank.

asks: what do I do in fights as a mage support
do I go for damage or stay back
who do I hit in teamfights
how do I teamfight with a damage support
say: Hit whoever walks into range first from the back, or save your crowd control for their diver if your carry's being chased.
more: You're a second damage source without a carry's items, so you can't afford to walk forward for the perfect target.
Damage on their front line still counts. It forces them back or makes the next engage cheaper.
Your one piece of crowd control is often the only peel your team has, so think before spending it on poke.
check: Does your team have another source of peel, and who is their main threat?
breaks: Wrong if their carry is the one out of position: then use everything on him, because a caught carry ends the fight.

when: your bot laner has the most kills on your team
asks: my adc is fed, what do I do
how do I play with a fed adc
adc's carrying, do I still engage
protect the adc or go in
say: Stay beside him and peel so he can keep hitting, or engage only when the target's already within his range.
more: When one player holds your team's lead, the whole fight is about how long he stays alive.
Every enemy will try to reach him. Your crowd control on them is worth more than a pick somewhere else.
Vision goes around him too: ward the flanks of wherever he's farming or sieging.
check: Where is he standing, and which enemy is most likely to dive him?
breaks: Wrong if he's in base or far from the fight: don't start anything until he's there.

when: your bot laner has more deaths than kills and less CS than their bot laner
asks: my adc is useless
adc's behind, who do I help
do I still stay with my adc
my carry is feeding what do I do
say: Play around whichever teammate has the most items, or stay with your marksman while he farms if nobody else is strong.
more: A support isn't tied to the bot laner after lane. Your abilities do the most on the player doing the most damage.
That might be a fed mid or top. Peeling or engaging for them wins fights a weak marksman can't.
If nobody's ahead, helping him farm safely is the long plan: marksmen come back with items.
check: Who on your team has the most kills and finished items?

elder or baron

more: Elder decides fights for as long as the buff lasts, so it's worth nearly everything.
At the pit, removing their jungler at the last moment is the surest way to win it.
Walking in one at a time loses the dragon and the players. Baron on the other side at least pays you back.
check: Are all five of you alive and close, and is baron up?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler is dead: don't trade, go straight to elder, because nobody can steal it.
basis: pro:If you cannot win the Smite duel, remove their jungler

when: an inhibitor of yours is down
asks: super minions are coming, what do I do
we lost an inhib, where do I go
should I defend base
inhib's down, do I leave
say: Stay with whoever clears the super minions and ward your base entrances, or group for baron once that wave's dead.
more: Super minions pin someone in base. The enemy uses that to take baron or elder with a numbers advantage.
Your wards around the base entrances stop the dive on the player clearing.
Clear the wave early, then move as five. Leaving while the wave is alive loses towers.
check: Who's clearing the wave, and what objective is up?
breaks: Wrong if your wave-clear champion handles it alone safely: go with the other three so the team isn't short at the objective.

when: their team has more kills, towers and dragons than yours
asks: we're losing, what do I do as support
how do I help when we're behind
how do we come back
game's going bad, support plan
say: Light up your own jungle so carries can farm, and wait for someone to overstep, or group at soul-point dragon.
more: A team that's behind comes back through farm and one caught enemy, not through even fights.
Your wards make both possible. They keep carries alive on their camps and show who walked too deep.
Early dragons can be given. The one that would give them soul is the fight you plan for.
check: How many dragons do they have, and which of your carries is closest to an item?
breaks: Wrong if they're taking towers for free while you wait: someone has to clear waves, so stand with that player.
basis: pro:Give early dragons, then fight the one before soul point

when: your team is behind and a dragon that is not their soul point is due
asks: we're behind, do we fight for dragon
should we contest drake when losing
do we give dragon
dragon's up and we're losing
say: Give it and take a tower or camps on the other side, or contest only if their jungler or a carry is dead.
more: Fighting an objective a full item behind usually loses the dragon and several players.
A conceded dragon is cheap if you get something back at the same time.
Your job is to make the trade safe: ward the side you're going to and ping it early.
check: Is anything worth taking on the far side, and who's dead on their team?
breaks: Wrong if nothing can be taken elsewhere: then just stay alive and clear waves rather than force a trade that isn't there.
basis: pro:Do not fight an objective one spike behind

when: your team is behind in kills and towers
asks: how do I get picks when behind
can I still engage when we're losing
should I go for a hook
we're behind, do I look for plays
say: Engage only on someone alone in your own jungle with teammates beside you, or hold your abilities and defend under tower.
more: A team ahead gets careless and walks into your side to ward or steal camps. That one player is your comeback.
In your own jungle your team arrives first and your wards see the reply coming.
Engaging onto their grouped team from behind just starts a fight you lose.
check: Is the target really alone, and who's close enough to follow you?
breaks: Wrong if the rest of their team is right behind him as bait: let him go and keep the tower.
basis: pro:When ahead, let them come to you

when: your team is behind in kills and towers
asks: enchanter when behind, what do I do
we're losing, who do I protect
how do I play from behind as an enchanter
who do I shield when we're losing
say: Stay with the carry who's closest to his next item while he farms, or follow the team's one strong player.
more: Coming back needs one teammate to reach a real power level. Your job is to get him there alive.
Standing with him on side waves and camps stops the pick that would end it.
If someone's already strong despite the score, your spells on him are how you win one fight.
check: Which carry has the most CS and items on your team?
breaks: Wrong if that player keeps walking into the enemy alone: you can't save that, so stay with a carry who plays safe.

when: your team is behind in kills and towers
asks: mage support when behind
we're losing, do I just clear waves
how do I stall as support
what do I do as a damage support when behind
say: Clear waves from range so towers don't fall while carries farm, or poke anyone who steps up to siege.
more: Wave clear is how a losing team buys time. Every wave that dies before the tower is time for your carries.
Poke on a sieging team makes them back off or dive at low health.
Don't walk forward for the last spell on a wave. Being caught while clearing is how sieges end.
check: Which tower are they pushing, and can anyone reach you where you stand?
breaks: Wrong if they're taking baron while you clear mid: ping it and move with the team or take a trade.

when: game time is past 20:00, baron is alive and your team is behind in kills and towers
asks: they're doing baron, do we go
baron's being taken, what do I do
do we contest baron when behind
should I check baron
say: Go only if all five walk in together, or push a side wave and take a tower while they're in the pit.
more: Arriving one at a time lets them kill your jungler first and then pick off the rest.
If you can't arrive as a group, a tower or dragon during their baron is real payment.
As support, don't be the one who walks up to look. Use a ward from range if you have one.
check: How many teammates are alive and near you, and where are the side waves?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler is dead: then a steal attempt with your jungler is worth the walk.
basis: pro:Arrive together or do not arrive

when: you are two or more levels below their support
asks: I'm way underleveled
I'm so behind on levels
how do I catch up as support
their support's way higher level than me
say: Stand near a side wave with a carry to soak experience for a few minutes, or stay grouped if an objective's close.
more: Supports fall behind in levels by roaming and dying. A level gap means weaker spells and less health when the fight comes.
Sharing a wave gives you experience without taking the gold, and keeps that carry safer too.
Avoid early fights where the level gap matters most, until an ultimate rank or key item closes it.
check: Which carry is farming a side lane, and what spawns in the next minute?
breaks: Wrong if your team needs vision for an objective right now: the wards come first, catch up after.
basis: pro:Early on, a level is worth more than a little gold

when: you have more deaths than anyone on your team
asks: I keep dying
I'm feeding as support
how do I stop getting caught
I've died too much, what now
say: Stop walking anywhere alone and ward only beside teammates, or sit on your carry and just use abilities from behind.
more: Most support deaths aren't in fights. They're on the walk to a ward or back to lane through dark jungle.
Each one gives gold and leaves your team a player short at the next objective.
A support who simply stays alive next to the carry is already useful. Build back from there.
check: Before every move: how many enemies are showing on the map?
breaks: Wrong if you're dying as the engager while your team follows and wins: those are good deaths, keep doing it.

when: your team is behind and you have little gold
asks: what do I buy when behind
I have no gold as support
behind, do I buy wards or items
what should I get, we're losing
say: Buy a control ward and the cheapest part of an item that protects your carry, or boots if you're still without them.
more: When you're poor, small purchases that work immediately beat saving for something large.
A control ward in your own jungle protects farm for minutes.
Defensive items for your carry are worth more than damage for you while you're behind.
check: What is your carry dying to, and do you have a control ward on the map already?
breaks: Wrong if you're a few gold from finishing a full item: wait one more wave and complete it.
